description: Transactions whose amount exceeds mean + 6 standard deviations (cutoff=$1,685,492.66, mean=$77,909.84, std=$267,930.47). These are not necessarily invalid (large legitimate wires exist) but are flagged for analyst review since they can dominate SUM-based KPIs.
Rows with a NULL value in any column that every downstream component (SQL aggregation, graph engine, feature builder) requires to be present.

tx_id is the primary key; this counts rows beyond the first for any tx_id that appears more than once. Because tx_id is PRIMARY KEY, true duplicates cannot exist post-insert -- a non-zero count here would indicate a schema/constraint failure, so this check exists as a defensive tripwire, not because duplicates are expected.

Distinct tx_ids that nonetheless share identical (source_entity, dest_entity, amount, currency, timestamp) -- the same economic event recorded twice, which would double-count volume and value KPIs if not flagged.

Transactions with amount <= 0. A financial transaction with zero or negative value is not a valid transfer in this model (refunds/reversals are out of scope for this dataset) and would distort every downstream sum/avg/VaR-style aggregate.
Currency codes outside the 7 configured in GEN_CFG.currencies: ['AED', 'CHF', 'EUR', 'GBP', 'HKD', 'SGD', 'USD'].
src_jurisdiction or dst_jurisdiction outside the 14 configured jurisdictions.
Transactions where source_entity equals dest_entity. An entity moving funds to itself is not economically meaningful and is either a generator defect or a data entry error.
Timestamps that do not parse as valid SQLite datetime values (strftime returns NULL for anything unparseable).
Transactions timestamped after the current UTC time -- a transaction cannot be recorded before it happens.
pattern_type outside the 6 labels the generator and evaluation pipeline recognise: ['circular_flow', 'high_risk_jx', 'layering', 'normal', 'structuring', 'velocity_burst'].
inter_arrival_s (seconds since the entity's previous transaction) is negative, which is only possible if rows were inserted out of generation order.
Alerts whose tx_id has no matching row in transactions -- a referential-integrity violation that would make an alert impossible to investigate (no source transaction to inspect).
source_entity or dest_entity is an empty string or whitespace-only -- distinct from NULL (covered by null_required_fields) but equally unusable for graph construction.
